basis: Perivascular epithelioid cell neoplasm arising in the lung.
Hereditary colorectal neoplastic susceptibility; colorectal target defines the axis, without implying existing cancer or damage.
Immune-mediated lichen planus with skin blistering; common damaging oral involvement is not established for this variant.
Motor neuron degeneration with defining muscle atrophy and diaphragmatic paralysis (11/11); respiratory failure reflects denervation rather than intrinsic lung damage.
Familial ligament calcification/ossification; suprascapular nerve entrapment is reported, but its frequency is insufficiently established for inclusion.
Salivary glands belong to the gastrointestinal axis; immune mechanisms apply only to some subtypes.
Autoimmune interstitial lung disease and inflammatory arthritis define the syndrome; renal disease is variably reported near or below 30%, so omitted.
Respiratory ciliary dysfunction causes chronic airway disease; recurrent middle-ear inflammation affects 31/35 (~89%), supporting otologic involvement.
Tumour originates in the fallopian tube, a reproductive organ outside the axes; smooth muscle origin does not imply skeletal muscle disease.
Sexual performance disorder confined to reproductive function; no specific endocrine, vascular or neurologic disease is established.
Pathologic calcium deposition classified as a calcium metabolic disorder; affected tissues vary across subtypes, without a common additional organ.
Carcinoma originates in the stomach; salivary gland type describes its histology.
Inner-ear labyrinth disease causing sensorineural hearing loss and vestibular dysfunction.
Extraembryonic membrane and placental disorders are obstetric and outside the axes; infection is not universal across this umbrella.
Inherited interstitial lung disease with parenchymal abnormalities and impaired gas transfer; clubbing does not establish another damaged organ.
Congenital joint contractures and limb abnormalities define the umbrella; neurologic causes are not shared across all major subtypes.
Inherited selective inability to perceive freesia odour; smell belongs to the neurologic axis.
Congenital bilateral absence of the lower limbs.
Intradural spinal arachnoid cysts occupy the spinal compartment and may compress the spinal cord or nerves.
Malignant neoplasm originating in the cervical oesophagus.
Deficient gonadotropin and sex-hormone production defines the disease; anosmia is not established as common in this KISS1 subtype.
Brain malformation and developmental impairment define this subtype; oculomotor apraxia and hyperventilation are central neurologic manifestations.
Severe hippocampal neuronal loss and gliosis are intrinsic brain pathology.
Isolated developmental eye malformation comprising microphthalmia and coloboma.
Congenital secondary erythrocytosis is a blood-cell disorder; vascular complications are not established as common defining involvement.
